text: P508323 - Indonesia Productive and Sustainable Investment DPL; Program Document PD000168 (2025-05-07), http://documents.worldbank.org/curated/en/099051325121035302. A stand-alone (not programmatic) IBRD loan of US$1.5 billion; implementing agency the Coordinating Ministry of Economic Affairs; overall risk Moderate (pp. 5-6, 9). Development objective: to mobilize finance and enable markets for productive, sustainable and resilient investment (p. 5).
Prior actions (discussed pp. 18-25; matrix in Annex 1, pp. 32-33):

Pillar A - mobilizing finance: 1. OJK raised the maximum loan ceiling for peer-to-peer lenders (OJK Regulation 40/2024) to increase MSME finance through digital financial services. 2. OJK enabled innovative credit scoring services (OJK Regulation 29/2024). 3. The Government transferred regulation and supervision of securities-based financial derivatives to OJK (Government Regulation 49/2024), and OJK put that authority into effect (OJK Regulation 1/2025). 4. OJK set a framework for climate-risk analysis and management in banks (CRMS Guidelines). 5. The Ministry of Finance set up a mechanism to collect, invest and disburse resources of the Disaster Pooling Fund (the matrix cites it as '[MOF regulation #28]').

Pillar B - enabling markets: 6. Eased local-content requirements for renewable energy power projects (MOI Regulations 33/2024 and 34/2024, MEMR Regulation 11/2024 and a MEMR decree). 7. A regulatory framework for environmentally sustainable practices in industrial estates (Government Regulation 20/2024). 8. A land value capture mechanism to recover and reinvest land-value gains from public infrastructure (Presidential Regulation 79/2024).

Intended results, baseline (June 2024) to target (December 2026) (pp. 32-33): MSME credit as a share of peer-to-peer lending 32% to 55%, with 50% to female borrowers; MSME credit as a share of total credit 20.5% to 25%; listed security futures on the stock exchange 11 to 16; systemic commercial banks adopting climate-risk management policies 0% to 100%; share of 2024 Disaster Pooling Fund resources used for active risk-transfer solutions 0% to 5%; reduction in the cost of renewable energy procurement 0% to 15%; industrial estates with environmental management systems 25% to 45% and with disaster early-warning systems 20% to 40%; private capital identified through land value capture US$0 to US$250 million.
The document estimates that PA 1 and PA 2 together could create about 0.7 million more and better jobs by 2026 (p. 18). These are targets at approval, not achieved results.
